pharm: Alpha-glucosidase inhibitor; delays intestinal carbohydrate digestion to blunt postprandial glucose rise
quick: 0.2 mg PO three times daily before meals; may increase to 0.3 mg TID
Safety not established; avoid unless clearly needed
Avoid; safety in lactation not established
Monitor liver enzymes; caution in hepatic impairment
summary: Voglibose is an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor used in Japan and India to control postprandial hyperglycemia in type 2 diabetes. It reversibly inhibits intestinal alpha-glucosidases, delaying carbohydrate digestion and slowing glucose absorption. It is not FDA-approved; this record is pending review.
indications: Improvement of postprandial hyperglycemia in diabetes mellitus (used with diet/exercise, alone or with other antidiabetic agents)
Prevention of progression to type 2 diabetes in patients with impaired glucose tolerance (Japanese labeling)

dosage.d: 0.2 mg three times daily; may increase to 0.3 mg three times daily if response is inadequate
dosage.t: Immediately before each meal (breakfast, lunch, dinner)
dosage.n: Maximum 0.3 mg per dose three times daily

admin: Administer immediately before each main meal for effect on that meal
If a meal is skipped, skip the corresponding dose
Counsel patients on management of hypoglycemia when combined with other antidiabetic drugs
moa: Voglibose reversibly inhibits alpha-glucosidase enzymes (such as maltase, sucrase, and isomaltase) in the brush border of the small intestine. This delays the breakdown of complex carbohydrates and disaccharides into absorbable monosaccharides, slowing glucose absorption and thereby reducing the postprandial rise in blood glucose. It does not stimulate insulin secretion.

relative: Conditions predisposing to intestinal obstruction (e.g., severe adhesions, prior abdominal surgery)

preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established. Use only if the expected benefit outweighs the potential risk; insulin is generally preferred for glycemic control in pregnancy.
lact: Use during breastfeeding is generally not recommended as safety has not been established; animal data suggest excretion into milk.
renal: Limited data in renal impairment; voglibose is minimally absorbed systemically, but use with caution and monitor in patients with significant renal impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment. Rare reports of hepatic dysfunction and jaundice; monitor liver enzymes and discontinue if significant abnormalities occur.

major: Insulin and sulfonylureas (increased risk of hypoglycemia when combined)
moderate: Drugs affecting glucose metabolism (e.g., corticosteroids, thiazides) may reduce efficacy
minor: Intestinal adsorbents and digestive enzyme preparations may reduce voglibose effect
interactions.food: Must be taken immediately before meals; efficacy depends on co-ingestion with carbohydrate-containing food
interactions.alcohol: Use with caution; alcohol may increase gastrointestinal side effects and affect glucose control
interactions.diagnostics: No specific laboratory test interference established

serious: Severe hypoglycemia when combined with insulin or sulfonylureas
emergency: Severe hypoglycemia - treat with oral glucose (dextrose), not sucrose, since disaccharide breakdown is inhibited
Ileus presenting with severe abdominal pain, distension, and vomiting

monitoring: Signs of hypoglycemia when used with insulin or sulfonylureas
counsel: Take immediately before each meal; if you skip a meal, skip that dose
Gas, bloating, and diarrhea are common early on and usually lessen over time
If using with other diabetes medicines and you have low blood sugar, use glucose (dextrose) tablets rather than table sugar, which works slower with this drug
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, or persistent abdominal pain
Continue diet and exercise as advised
pk: Acts during the meal it is taken with (postprandial)
Maximal enzyme inhibition during digestion; minimal systemic absorption
Short; drug acts locally in the gut with very low systemic exposure
Effect limited to the period of carbohydrate digestion of the accompanying meal
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light
pearls: Targets postprandial glucose specifically rather than fasting glucose
Does not cause hypoglycemia as monotherapy because it does not stimulate insulin
When hypoglycemia occurs with combination therapy, treat with glucose (dextrose), not sucrose
Gastrointestinal side effects are dose-related; titrate and counsel patients
Not FDA-approved; used in Japan and India - record pending review
missed: Voglibose is only effective when taken just before a meal. If a dose is missed before or during a meal, skip it and take the next dose before the following meal. Do not take a dose between meals or double up.
overdose: Overdose is expected to cause exaggerated gastrointestinal effects such as flatulence, diarrhea, and abdominal discomfort, as systemic absorption is minimal. Severe hypoglycemia is unlikely with voglibose alone but may occur with concomitant insulin or sulfonylureas; treat with oral or intravenous glucose (dextrose). Management is supportive.
